acceptance.evidence: test/index.test.js 'AC-1' checks seed rows, UNIQUE, CHECK, nullable column, index, and tagged items; migrations/0003 matches.
test 'AC-2' covers a title-only insert (null category) and a FOREIGN KEY rejection.
test 'AC-3' checks id order, the labelled markup and the unlabelled <li>.
test 'AC-4' checks the link order (case-insensitive), hrefs, a category with no items, and All being the only current link.
Two 'AC-5' tests cover the Work-only list, current link, and the &x=1 and ?x=1 equivalences.
test 'AC-6' checks the 200 status, the message, no <li>, and the current link.
test 'AC-7' checks the escaping, the encoded href, and that following the link lists the item.
test.each 'AC-8' covers all five URLs: 404, message, Go back link, script, no <li> and no <nav>.

This is a review-only browser step and I could not run a browser. The script also adds an unspecified `history.length > 1` condition. The spec's step 'navigate to /?category=Wrok' is ambiguous: typing the URL leaves no referrer, so it would land on / and not on Home. Nothing in the repo demonstrates the flow.

routes.json lists the route. tests/traffic-config.test.sh accepts a query route and rejects whitespace, '#' and a missing slash. test/traffic.test.js records path plus query. The 'AC-11' test in index.test.js checks that every listed route answers 2xx.
The existing healthz, 404, 405, h1 and 'No items yet.' tests remain, and the First item assertion is updated to the AC-3 markup. Those tests are not named AC-12 in their titles.
apply-migrations.js drops the tables in a batch with deferred foreign keys. The 'AC-13' test adds a categorised row and checks that the reset happened (count is 4).

findings.what: The Go back handler goes back only if the referrer is same-origin AND `history.length > 1`. The spec's decision says same-origin referrer alone, and it rejects `history.length > 1` as a criterion. AC-10 has no demonstrated browser evidence.
findings.fix: Drop the `history.length > 1` condition, or record the owner's call in the spec. Run the AC-10 steps in a browser and note the result.

findings.what: The state-table rows for 200 pages (Go back hidden, filter links shown on an empty table) are not asserted. The existing 'No items yet.' test only checks the message. AC-12's existing tests are not named by AC id.
findings.fix: In the 'No items yet.' test and the 200 tests, also assert that the nav is present and that no 'Go back' link is shown. Name the AC-12 tests.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's decisions, apart from the extra history.length condition in Go back.
The spec's go is recorded in a commit before the implementation. No acceptance item was edited after the go.
Tests cover AC-1 to AC-9, AC-11 and AC-13, and would fail against broken code. I did not run the suite here; CI runs it.
The README is updated for the filter and the 404 on a bad link.
The queries are parameterised, and the handling of an empty or repeated category value is correct.
Names are HTML-escaped and URL-encoded and SQL is bound. I found no instructions planted in the content.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or stylesheet files; the review cannot cover design in a browser.
A browser flow exists only for AC-10, which is review-only, and I could not run a browser.
